The economy moves from the old intersection of aggregate demand
and aggregate supply, point A, to the new intersection, point B. The movement
from point A to point B represents a decline in output at a ﬁxed price level.
Thus, a fall in aggregate demand reduces output in the short run because
prices do not adjust instantly. After the sudden fall in aggregate demand, ﬁrms
are stuck with prices that are too high. With demand low and prices high, ﬁrms
